Windsor, as she introduced herself, reminded Alito that she had spoken with him a year earlier at the same event and wanted to ask him the same question. "What I asked you about was about the polarization in this country, about, like, how do we repair that rift?" she asked. "And considering everything that's been going on in the past year, you know, as a Catholic, and as someone who really cherishes my faith, I just don't -- I don't know that we can negotiate with the left in the way that needs to happen for the polarization to end. I think it is a matter of like, winning."
"I think you're probably right," Alito said, before delving into his analysis that "one side or the other is going to win," a zero-sum approach to political warfare. Windsor also spoke with Chief Justice John Roberts that evening, and the stark difference between the two answers was remarkable. Roberts rejected Windsor's premise, suggesting that it is not the job of the Court to dictate morality.
Alito, meanwhile, agreed with Windsor that believers need to fight "to return our country to a place of godliness."
"I think that the solution really is winning the moral argument," Windsor said. "People in this country who believe in God have got to keep fighting for that, to return our country to a place of godliness."
"Oh, I agree with you. I agree with you," Alito said.
Windsor in the past has been criticized by conservatives for leading her interlocutors on, but her conversation with Roberts shows that Alito easily had other directions to take the question. "I believe that the founders were godly, were Christians, and I think that we live in a Christian nation, and that our Supreme Court should be guiding us in that path," Windsor said, as Roberts cut her off.
"I don't know if that's true," he said. "I don't know that we live in a Christian nation. I know a lot of Jewish and Muslim friends who would say maybe not, and it's not our job to do that. It's our job to decide the cases as best we can."
Roberts also argued that it was not unusual for the court to be in the middle of heated cultural and political battles. "With everything that's going on right now, it's a very tumultuous time in the country. And I'm just curious, from your perspective on the court, how do we start to repair the polarization?" Windsor asked.
"The first thing I think is to tell me when the non-tumultuous time has been here," he said. "I mean, you're looking at the court -- what the court was doing in the '60s, what the court was doing during the New Deal, what the court was doing, you know, after Dred Scott and all this. It's kind of a regular thing. People think it's so different and special. It's been pretty tumultuous for a long time. Vietnam."
"So you think this is a normal period?" she asked.
"You know, I don't know if it's normal," he responded. "I mean, since I've been here all of 20 years, there've been quieter times. But the idea that the court is in the middle of a lot of tumultuous stuff going on, that's nothing new."
"I guess I just really feel like we're at a point in our country where the polarization is so extreme that it might be irreparable," Windsor told him, and Roberts interrupted.
"Oh I don't think that. Polarization that's extreme is like the Civil War," he said, adding that the Vietnam era was also intense. "People with their own perspective think this is so extraordinary. Eh, I don't know."
"You don't think there's like a role for the court in, like, guiding us toward a more moral path?" Windsor asked.
"No, I think the role of the court is deciding the cases," he said. "Would you want me to be in charge of guiding us toward a more moral path? That's for the people we elect. That's not for lawyers."
Alito has been under fire for having flown [two flags](https://substack.com/redirect/669be4d0-d60e-47a6-9ade-f51f42c34233?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)[ associated with](https://substack.com/redirect/21267ca4-8be1-4fa1-9c13-2f79387a9815?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) insurrectionary elements of the far right. He blamed one of them on his wife.
Windsor attended the reception under her real name and introduced herself to Alito as Lauren, reminding him they had spoken the year before. A year earlier, Alito had been more cautious in his answers to Windsor, sounding more like Roberts than the radicalized contemporary Alito.
Windsor, at the 2023 reception, had asked Alito how we could repair the polarization rifts in the country. "I don't think it's something we can do. We have a very defined role," he said of the court. "We need to do what we're supposed to do. But this is a bigger problem. This is way above us. I wish I knew the answer."
Alito is under significant pressure to recuse himself as the Supreme Court weighs whether to grant former President Trump immunity from prosecution. In fact,[ there's a petition urging him to recuse from the case that readers can sign here](https://substack.com/redirect/da8c8094-17cf-4408-bec6-6ba543ccf5c8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). A ruling in the case is expected before the end of the month.

_Wesley Hunt here._

As we head into another election year, I want to ensure that the generous people supporting my reelection know why I'm running.

I was born and raised in Houston, Texas.

After graduating from high school, I felt the call to serve our nation in the military, like my father and sister before me, and I accepted an appointment to the United States Military Academy at West Point.
[](http://links.wesleyhunttx.com/u/click?_t=6aa969a792e549699e2a6024aa3e4ace&_m=911cf32435b34c7588cbacb9fcba3251&_e=cZ1PBswE8740Y940JiV-aalZTOPCRtuV5ez29bb03OiDN6OjS7hHYxEvROayI4kAYgzMUR_AGCylOKnPqeT64omuks5yI3zz3OQHqx90oHpA6OSW4sYkeriAJqUHv8PBIX7uSjj21m8ul10ymveCtDqHW3dKifMFtMTcD50sx8Pe5s4IZjhsYgrqJHu4GngEdI8IEv78O_NuTjHkhCctgAfz8jKW-Q8ThTdDi_QEnN02JHVCFpDdQMCnuECXgh_E1ArRJLm-hXq85uJ71arMg3B07-mrCAktKt6iPEbLJRM%3D)_
(Me with my brother and sister, who also attended West Point)_
My service included one combat deployment to Iraq and two to Saudi Arabia, where I served as a Diplomatic Liaison Officer. While in Saudi Arabia, I represented the U.S. government in missions involving the Royal Saudi Land Forces Aviation Corps.

After completing my military service, I attended Cornell University, where I earned a Master of Business Administration (M.B.A.), a Master of Public Administration (M.P.A.), and a Master of Industrial and Labor Relations (M.I.L.R.).

I never thought I would get involved in politics, but after seeing the dysfunction and destruction wrought by liberal elites in the Democrat party, I was once again called to serve our great nation, by running for the United States Congress.

I knew that challenging the DC Washington elite wouldn't be easy, but after flying Apache helicopters over Iraq, I knew I was prepared to take on the tough fights.

****Join me in the fight to save the future of America.****

[](http://links.wesleyhunttx.com/u/click?_t=6aa969a792e549699e2a6024aa3e4ace&_m=911cf32435b34c7588cbacb9fcba3251&_e=cZ1PBswE8740Y940JiV-aalZTOPCRtuV5ez29bb03OiDN6OjS7hHYxEvROayI4kAYgzMUR_AGCylOKnPqeT64omuks5yI3zz3OQHqx90oHpA6OSW4sYkeriAJqUHv8PBIX7uSjj21m8ul10ymveCtDcDA6F006mydH09EDfMdayU5XWO7_NVP00x3iq4m1NyyaAdOHuHaDp1VkHaCpS3f1VMDNqROWv7zkSrfr49AjQwQyjI60Vb8SOFoYz1PiSDQhBNx77BFWSyFZPiItCVmIatb1zONZ7M5WyCf9dQ094%3D)

Now, here we are in one of the most consequential election years of our lifetime. The majority we fought so hard for in 2022 hangs in the balance, and conservative ideals are under fire every day.

name: Sen. Kirsten Gillibrand
subject: a lesson my grandmother taught me
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Gillibrand for Senate
body:
she showed me how campaigns are won
| | |
---
Look, big change starts small.
That's a lesson that my grandmother, Polly Noonan, first taught me decades ago. Well before most women had any political power, my grandmother organized women into a political force in Albany.
By the time I was in elementary school, I was tagging along with her to all kinds of Democratic campaign headquarters, rallies and events. She remains one of my biggest role models — and I carry her wisdom with me to this day. **She taught me that my voice matters, that women’s voices matter and that grassroots activism matters. And she showed me how campaigns are won by the people who put in the work like the volunteers knocking doors, stuffing envelopes, turning out the vote and donating what they can, when they can.**
For decades, first by my grandmother's side and then as a public servant myself, I've seen how those small grassroots actions all add up to victory on Election Day. That's how Democrats defeated the odds in 2022 to defend and even expand our Senate majority. And that's why I know that we can win again in 2024.
With Democrats defending 23 seats, the odds are certainly stacked against us. And after the 2022 red wave in New York, Republicans here are already targeting my seat for defeat. **But when people like you get off the sidelines and chip in even just $3, eventually we'll build a grassroots movement capable of defeating even the GOP's wealthiest megadonors.**
**[So please, will you chip in $3 or $25 or whatever you can spare today to help save our Senate majority by building a grassroots movement one grassroots gift at a time? June 10th Newsletter + VMSDEP Update
Dear neighbors,
School is out for summer and we’ve made it almost halfway through 2024! Can you believe it? The weather certainly knows it. A reminder to sunscreen up and protect your skin while you enjoy this sunny season.
But June doesn’t just mean summer, it also means primary election season. Whoever you decide to vote for, I hope you make a plan to vote in our June 18th Primary. Polls will be open from 6am to 7pm. As long as you are in line by 7pm on election day you will be able to vote, but you don’t have to wait until election day to do your civic duty.
In-person early voting is happening now at your local registrar's office. The last day of in-person early voting at your local voter registration office is Saturday, June 15, 2024 at 5:00 p.m. See who is on your ballot by viewing the candidate lists here [https://www.elections.virginia.gov/casting-a-ballot/candidate-list/] . Register to vote or apply for an absentee ballot online using the Citizen Portal here [https://www.elections.virginia.gov/citizen-portal/] .
General Assembly Updates
Prince William County Virtual Town Hall | Recording Available: On June 4th at 7pm members of your Prince William County General Assembly delegation got together to discuss legislative updates and answer questions from constituents. If you missed it, you can check out the zoom recording here [https://drive.google.com/file/d/1T0q1U7DXUPxHHITcfJjXeF31jPAxFEGe/view?usp=drive_link] . [https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/NGP/NGP13/1/87444/images/Screenshot%202024-05-23%20at%201.39.13%20PM.png]
Issue of the Week - The Virginia Military Survivors and Dependents Education Program (VMSDEP)
The 2024-2026 biennial Virginia budget HB6001 which was passed on a bipartisan basis on May 13th during the 2024-2025 legislative session involved some changes to the VMSDEP programs to ensure its sustainability and financial support for these educational waivers for years to come.
I am proud to represent a district where more than 20% of all residents are veterans compared to veterans being only 8% of the Virginia population. Of the 18,426 constituents of mine who are veterans, more than a 100 have been VMSDEP recipients. This program has enabled many in our community to go to college debt-free. The sacrifice of our veterans cannot be overstated and we cannot overstate the debt we owe in Virginia to the families that have served.
As the daughter of two Air Force veterans, I take this debt of service very seriously, and have been and continue to be a steadfast advocate for access to these benefits in my role as a member of the House Appropriations Committee. I also believe strongly that in order to conduct good government, we have to create programs that are sustainable and can continue for generations to come. Below is a detailed accounting of the history of the VMSDEP policy, the changes over time.
History of VMSDEP
The VMSDEP program was initially started in the 1930’s to support the education of soldiers returning from World War I. At that time it was an appropriations based program available to all children of veterans ages 16-25. Eligible students had parents who were killed or totally and permanently disabled and students had to show satisfactory academic progress to maintain the scholarship.
The program has undergone many iterative changes since, including many changes to the benefit in the 70’s and 80’s, post-9/11, and most recently in 2019. The gradual expansion of benefits included changes to the Virginia residency requirement, eligibility of spouses, and expansion of benefits to veterans whose disability status was 90% totally and permanently disabled.
In the 2000’s the benefit shifted from being appropriations based (meaning students were given scholarships from the state) to waiver-based, meaning public universities were expected to forgo tuition and fee payments for eligible VMSDEP students and make up costs through other means.
Although this shift limited the cost liability of the program to the state general fund, it shifted the weight of the costs of the program to the universities who made up the funds through raising costs of tuition and fees across all other tuition paying students (most of whom live in state). This change was considered manageable because at the time the change was made, the overall cost of the program and the total quantity of students was low and not increasing. You can see in the graph below that the rate of students enrolled via VMSDEP was relatively stable.
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/NGP/NGP13/1/87444/images/Screenshot%202024-06-10%20at%2012.19.12%20PM.png]
All this changed in 2019. Expansion to the waiver program granted more student eligibility for the VMSDEP waiver and costs began to skyrocket. See the change in the VMSDEP recipients and the cost to universities below.
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/NGP/NGP13/1/87444/images/Screenshot%202024-06-10%20at%2012.19.21%20PM.png]
Changes to the Program
To contain the cost of the program and ensure the sustainability of the waiver and stipends, HB6001, the 2024-2026 budget bill included some changes to VMSDEP eligibility. These changes included limiting the award to students pursuing their first undergraduate degree, requiring academic progress as a condition of the award, and retaining a Virginia domicile requirement for students versus a simple presence in the state. The most substantial change and that which has sparked concern from many who benefit from this program is the change in first and last dollars. Under new VMSDEP requirements, all VMSDEP-eligible students must apply to the FAFSA. Depending on their expected family contribution (or EFC), students will be required to contribute either some of their Pell grant funds, or some of their own funds toward their tuition and fees before the waiver goes into effect. A brief summary of these changes are seen on the slide below:
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/NGP/NGP13/1/87444/images/Screenshot%202024-06-10%20at%2012.19.36%20PM.png]
This does not mean students must exhaust all federal funds before using the waiver, but rather they must spend a portion of their Pell scholarship or expected family contribution before using the waiver. The amount families will need to pay is based on the ratio between tuition and fees and total cost of attendance as well as their EFC according to the FAFSA. For example, a student attending a school where their tuition and fees equal $25K per year and their total cost of attendance is $50K per year would pay 50% of their Pell grant toward tuition before the waiver kicked in. Students not eligible for the pell grant would pay the same ratio out of pocket.
Now the VMSDEP waiver acts as a middle dollar after some federal funds are used but not exhausted. Students do not have to exhaust federal GI bill funds at all. They may choose to not bring these benefits to the table and the full waiver may still be applied.
You can see a comparison between the VMSDEP program pre-2019, 2019-2024, and now post-2024 side-by-side with similar states below.
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/NGP/NGP13/1/87444/images/Screenshot%202024-06-10%20at%2012.19.50%20PM.png]
My Promise
I have been meeting one-on-one with constituents who are concerned they may be affected by this policy for the last month and will continue to do so. I remain dedicated to being available to answer any questions and discuss concerns about these changes. I want to hear from you and I take your concerns extremely seriously. With that in mind, I hope this detailed, and at times, very technical, accounting of the changes to this program and what they mean for VMSDEP recipients across Virginia was helpful. I know there are still elements of the most recent set of policy changes that may have missed the mark. The VMSDEP task force convened by the governor will be meeting on June 10th to discuss these changes and consider making legislative recommendations to continue fine tuning this program in the 2025 legislative session. The Preserving VMSDEP Task Force will meet Monday, June 10 at 2 p.m. at the Virginia War Memorial. Members of the public are encouraged to join virtually here: https://us02web.zoom.us/j/87252153427 [https://us02web.zoom.us/j/87252153427] .
You can continue to learn more about the program by watching the full presentation made to the House Appropriations Committee on May 20th here [https://virginiageneralassembly.gov/house/chamber/chamberstream.php] . As of June 6th, the Speaker of the House has announced that we will reconvene 2024 Special Session I on Friday, June 28 at 10:00 AM to address the Virginia Military Survivors and Dependents Education Program. I look forward to working together with my colleagues across the aisle to address immediate concerns and remain committed to creating a sustainable solution.
In the meantime, my door is always open and you are welcome to schedule a meeting to talk to me about your specific VMSDEP story and how this program impacts you. My email is DelBSewell@house.virginia.gov [DelBSewell@house.virginia.gov] .
News You Can Use
End to no-strings-attached free checking raises concerns among some advocates for low-income residents [https://cardinalnews.org/2024/05/28/end-to-no-strings-attached-free-checking-raises-concerns-among-some-advocates-for-low-income-residents/] | Cardinal News
As Freedom First and other financial institutions have enacted new account minimums, they have raised concerns among some who argue that people with low incomes struggle to meet the requirements or pay the fees.
Why three Colonial-era newspapers in Williamsburg called themselves The Virginia Gazette — and even published at the same time [https://cardinalnews.org/2024/05/14/why-three-colonial-era-newspapers-in-williamsburg-called-themselves-the-virginia-gazette-and-even-published-at-the-same-time/] | Cardinal News
Untangling the history of Virginia’s first newspaper and the homonymous publications that followed, each with a claim to fame in the annals of journalism.
'That nation which respects and honors its dead, shall ever be respected and honored itself' [https://www.insidenova.com/headlines/that-nation-which-respects-and-honors-its-dead-shall-ever-be-respected-and-honored-itself/article_cfb13568-5103-56fc-bcd9-652e33344383.html] | InsideNOVA
Memorial Day, a federal holiday held the last Monday in May, is the nation's foremost annual day to mourn and honor its deceased service men and women.
Fort Belvoir honors Memorial Day with annual wreath-laying event [https://www.insidenova.com/headlines/fort-belvoir-honors-memorial-day-with-annual-wreath-laying-event/article_f6696910-19bc-11ef-96c8-071e646b78cf.html] | InsideNOVA
Fort Belvoir kicked off the holiday weekend early Thursday with a wreath-laying ceremony followed by a multi-part festival.
Prince William County Public Schools bids farewell to nearly 300 retiring employees [https://www.insidenova.com/headlines/prince-william-county-public-schools-bids-farewell-to-nearly-300-retiring-employees/article_36572294-1853-11ef-a32a-cb4abe177f93.html] | InsideNOVA
Prince William County Public Schools hosted a ceremony Tuesday to honor the nearly 300 employees retiring at the end of this school year.
As Memorial Day arrives, bill unveiled in Congress to assist Purple Heart recipients [https://virginiamercury.com/2024/05/27/as-memorial-day-arrives-bill-unveiled-in-congress-to-assist-purple-heart-recipients/] | Virginia Mercury
When a Purple Heart recipient named Pat reached out to U.S. Sen. Patty Murray in November to inform her that he couldn’t transfer his GI bill benefits to his children, he wasn’t expecting congressional action to solve the problem.
State, federal aid help Brown v. Board of Education scholarship fund reach over $3.4 million [https://virginiamercury.com/2024/05/23/state-federal-aid-help-brown-v-board-of-education-scholarship-fund-reach-over-3-4-million/] | Virginia Mercury
On the heels of the 70th anniversary of the Brown v. Board of Education ruling, which mandated public school desegregation nationwide, Virginia’s scholarship fund named after the landmark Supreme Court case has gained $2.5 million in federal and state aid.
Community Events

Sharron Baucom Dale City Recreation Center Dance Academy presents Graduation Ball, a lighthearted and fun ballet set to music by Johann Strauss including themed dances performed by recital students.

As long as you are in line by 7pm on election day you will be able to vote, but you don’t have to wait until election day to do your civic duty. In-person early voting is happening now at your local registrar's office. The last day of in-person early voting at your local voter registration office is Saturday, June 15, 2024 at 5:00 p.m. See who is on your ballot by viewing the candidate lists here [] . Register to vote or apply for an absentee ballot online using the Citizen Portal here [] . General Assembly Updates Prince William County Virtual Town Hall | Recording Available: On June 4th at 7pm members of your Prince William County General Assembly delegation got together to discuss legislative updates and answer questions from constituents. If you missed it, you can check out the zoom recording here [] . [] Issue of the Week - The Virginia Military Survivors and Dependents Education Program (VMSDEP) The 2024-2026 biennial Virginia budget HB6001 which was passed on a bipartisan basis on May 13th during the 2024-2025 legislative session involved some changes to the VMSDEP programs to ensure its sustainability and financial support for these educational waivers for years to come. I am proud to represent a district where more than 20% of all residents are veterans compared to veterans being only 8% of the Virginia population. Of the 18,426 constituents of mine who are veterans, more than a 100 have been VMSDEP recipients. This program has enabled many in our community to go to college debt-free. The sacrifice of our veterans cannot be overstated and we cannot overstate the debt we owe in Virginia to the families that have served. As the daughter of two Air Force veterans, I take this debt of service very seriously, and have been and continue to be a steadfast advocate for access to these benefits in my role as a member of the House Appropriations Committee. I also believe strongly that in order to conduct good government, we have to create programs that are sustainable and can continue for generations to come. Below is a detailed accounting of the history of the VMSDEP policy, the changes over time. History of VMSDEP The VMSDEP program was initially started in the 1930’s to support the education of soldiers returning from World War I. At that time it was an appropriations based program available to all children of veterans ages 16-25. Eligible students had parents who were killed or totally and permanently disabled and students had to show satisfactory academic progress to maintain the scholarship. The program has undergone many iterative changes since, including many changes to the benefit in the 70’s and 80’s, post-9/11, and most recently in 2019. The gradual expansion of benefits included changes to the Virginia residency requirement, eligibility of spouses, and expansion of benefits to veterans whose disability status was 90% totally and permanently disabled. In the 2000’s the benefit shifted from being appropriations based (meaning students were given scholarships from the state) to waiver-based, meaning public universities were expected to forgo tuition and fee payments for eligible VMSDEP students and make up costs through other means. Although this shift limited the cost liability of the program to the state general fund, it shifted the weight of the costs of the program to the universities who made up the funds through raising costs of tuition and fees across all other tuition paying students (most of whom live in state). This change was considered manageable because at the time the change was made, the overall cost of the program and the total quantity of students was low and not increasing. You can see in the graph below that the rate of students enrolled via VMSDEP was relatively stable. [] All this changed in 2019. Expansion to the waiver program granted more student eligibility for the VMSDEP waiver and costs began to skyrocket. See the change in the VMSDEP recipients and the cost to universities below. [] Changes to the Program To contain the cost of the program and ensure the sustainability of the waiver and stipends, HB6001, the 2024-2026 budget bill included some changes to VMSDEP eligibility. These changes included limiting the award to students pursuing their first undergraduate degree, requiring academic progress as a condition of the award, and retaining a Virginia domicile requirement for students versus a simple presence in the state. The most substantial change and that which has sparked concern from many who benefit from this program is the change in first and last dollars. Under new VMSDEP requirements, all VMSDEP-eligible students must apply to the FAFSA. Depending on their expected family contribution (or EFC), students will be required to contribute either some of their Pell grant funds, or some of their own funds toward their tuition and fees before the waiver goes into effect. A brief summary of these changes are seen on the slide below: [] This does not mean students must exhaust all federal funds before using the waiver, but rather they must spend a portion of their Pell scholarship or expected family contribution before using the waiver. The amount families will need to pay is based on the ratio between tuition and fees and total cost of attendance as well as their EFC according to the FAFSA. For example, a student attending a school where their tuition and fees equal $25K per year and their total cost of attendance is $50K per year would pay 50% of their Pell grant toward tuition before the waiver kicked in. Students not eligible for the pell grant would pay the same ratio out of pocket. Now the VMSDEP waiver acts as a middle dollar after some federal funds are used but not exhausted. Students do not have to exhaust federal GI bill funds at all. They may choose to not bring these benefits to the table and the full waiver may still be applied. You can see a comparison between the VMSDEP program pre-2019, 2019-2024, and now post-2024 side-by-side with similar states below. [] My Promise I have been meeting one-on-one with constituents who are concerned they may be affected by this policy for the last month and will continue to do so. I remain dedicated to being available to answer any questions and discuss concerns about these changes. I want to hear from you and I take your concerns extremely seriously. With that in mind, I hope this detailed, and at times, very technical, accounting of the changes to this program and what they mean for VMSDEP recipients across Virginia was helpful. I know there are still elements of the most recent set of policy changes that may have missed the mark. The VMSDEP task force convened by the governor will be meeting on June 10th to discuss these changes and consider making legislative recommendations to continue fine tuning this program in the 2025 legislative session. The Preserving VMSDEP Task Force will meet Monday, June 10 at 2 p.m. at the Virginia War Memorial. Members of the public are encouraged to join virtually here: [] . You can continue to learn more about the program by watching the full presentation made to the House Appropriations Committee on May 20th here [] . As of June 6th, the Speaker of the House has announced that we will reconvene 2024 Special Session I on Friday, June 28 at 10:00 AM to address the Virginia Military Survivors and Dependents Education Program. I look forward to working together with my colleagues across the aisle to address immediate concerns and remain committed to creating a sustainable solution. In the meantime, my door is always open and you are welcome to schedule a meeting to talk to me about your specific VMSDEP story and how this program impacts you. My email is DelBSewell@house.virginia.gov [DelBSewell@house.virginia.gov] . name: Bryan
subject: Campaign Update
body:
Happy Monday! Here’s an update of what I’ve been working on and how it impacts us here in Wisconsin. | | | | |
---
| Happy Monday!
Here’s an update of what I’ve been working on and how it impacts us here in Wisconsin.
**Bidenbucks in Wisconsin** I serve as the Chairman of the Committee on House Administration, which has broad oversight of our nation’s federal election law.
My latest efforts have focused on banning Bidenbucks from influencing our elections in Wisconsin.
Bidenbucks are taxpayer dollars that Joe Biden has authorized to be used by federal agencies to get-out-the-vote across the country. If left unchecked, taxpayer dollars could be used by partisan federal agencies in voter registration and ultimately influence our elections.
---
[Click Here to Learn More!](https://bryansteil.us18.list-manage.com/track/click?u=5855432ef30dec79be4122095&id=36970287b9&e=e907534017)
| Last week, I sent a letter to the President of the Universities of Wisconsin to ensure federal taxpayer dollars are not being used to fund partisan election efforts on UW campuses.
Elections are partisan, but election administration should never be partisan.
**Helping Racine County With Critical Water Infrastructure Projects** I’m working to secure federal funding to support necessary infrastructure projects in Racine County.
In 2020, winter storms caused significant damage to the Racine Harbor breakwater. Since then, the community has struggled to make necessary repairs to protect the historic downtown, the Lake Michigan shoreline, and the harbor from storms.
**That’s why I introduced a bill** that will open avenues for Racine and other community harbors to receive federal assistance for critical water infrastructure projects.
---
[Click Here to Learn More About My Bill!](https://bryansteil.us18.list-manage.com/track/click?u=5855432ef30dec79be4122095&id=078841d903&e=e907534017)
| **Non-Citizen Voting** Did you know that current law in Washington D.C. allows non-citizens to vote in local elections?
And what’s worse?
The Washington D.C. Board of Elections is actively encouraging non-citizens to vote in local elections.
As Chairman of the Committee on House Administration, I held a hearing to raise awareness of this practice and encourage my colleagues to support my legislation that bans non-citizens from voting in American elections.
---
[Click Here to Read More About My Hearing!](https://bryansteil.us18.list-manage.com/track/click?u=5855432ef30dec79be4122095&id=180384810a&e=e907534017)
| **Currently, the Wisconsin Constitution does not explicitly prohibit non-citizens from voting in Wisconsin.**
This November, the people of Wisconsin will vote on a constitutional ballot initiative to decide whether non-citizens should be allowed to vote in our state. I am hopeful voters will pass it.
Federal law currently bans non-citizens from voting in federal elections. However, federal law also makes it illegal to evade Border Patrol and illegally cross the border, yet that hasn’t stopped anyone from doing it.
My position is we should work to further enforce the federal non-citizen voting laws. Enforcement of the law is critical to increase integrity in our elections.

On Wisconsin,
Bryan Steil
---

Fellow Patriot,

My name is Robert Spencer. I'm an author, speaker, and expert on global Jihad and Islamic terrorism, and I wanted you to know how pro-Hamas forces are taking over higher education.

Recently, the University of California in Los Angeles (UCLA) blocked me from speaking to their students about Hamas' reign of terror through a Young America's Foundation (YAF) lecture. Instead of supporting free speech and open dialogue, UCLA administrators sided with radical leftist agitators and canceled the event.

UCLA's reason? They said that the ongoing pro-Hamas leftist supporters on the university grounds posed a safety hazard to the students who wanted to host and attend the event.

UCLA should have upheld law and order by clearing the encampments and prosecuting all violators to the fullest extent of the law.

**Instead, they took every available action to block me from speaking and to prevent their conservative students from exercising their First Amendment rights to freedom of speech and assembly. **

The organization that invited me to speak - Young America's Foundation - is suing UCLA for this blatant violation of freedom of speech. **[Give $50 right now to fight back and help sue UCLA!](http://links.newsletter.conservativedirect.com/u/click?_t=5b1853ae48754bee8f471363fe4933a9&_m=1fa28fdbba8946539844ceafdcd135dc&_e=HXPr2cPeK3fWc34pcmSCNUszHXapj1CmeXiHx8uiFuGMo4Gk6cRFdJVlSiSbDzRt2Nt4kV4XJrBl-3v-mF1SRw9QpNYfAAJHH6iajakHrQHacRXq1AP5H1t6dIMO6aYDKDNDfmPFtJ6Lw3uPyd4VL1PdD1b1t5WkFSScoe-JxVySsj5qDK6LsjzQqbETx-Dspl2hi1i45GNxYzjkKPljHagZW3n0j7qQ3W31IVlg48Lm7v4gFB53gBzuNXuHsD7oh41nDWhiunBo-QbqpJctXNYsWWQXk86X9ngrcIFujRYSD6cIHRWKLdzl_Q_ybyO-bxzWrwS7CGhYGad0SHEQ60AZlaMX_UpYHxgAX5da7UUYESMHzf9SYjCqgiM44KLS2AX80nc6TWeznZK6XokpCw%3D%3D)** Colleges are supposed to promote learning and dialogue, **not to provide sanctuary to radical agitators threatening Jewish students and Jihad on campus.** Yet, today, many have become sanctuaries for radical ideologies.

_All of this is having an effect on students ' opinions and attitudes today. _

Did you know that according to a recent NBC News poll, only 15% of young people ages 18-29 say their sympathies are with Israel, and nearly 1/3 of students say they sympathize with Palestinians?

In another poll, 20% of young Americans have a _positive_ view of Osama Bin Laden!

At UCLA (shortly before I was slated to deliver my speech there), pro-Hamas militants knocked a Jewish girl unconscious and stomped on her Israel flag. And there was no outrage over this by leftist administrators at the college.

Instead, a conservative coming to speak on campus is the UCLA administrators' greatest fear and the biggest security threat!

Enough is enough. We need your support to help YAF win this lawsuit against UCLA and help fight for students' free speech rights nationwide.

You may have heard of Young America's Foundation as the country's leading conservative youth organization for more than 60 years. YAF goes directly to high school and college campuses with the best speakers in the conservative movement, including **Ben Shapiro** , **Matt Walsh** , **Katie Pavlich** , Lt. Col. **Allen West** , and many others so that students can freely express and engage with the values that make us free. YAF promotes your values, such as a strong national defense, individual freedom, limited government, and freedom of speech to large student audiences.

Young America's Foundation is taking a stand against UCLA's censorship of conservative free speech.

**YAF is suing UCLA and will take them to court so that students can hear the truth about Hamas --the truth that their school is fighting to keep from them. **

But they can't do this alone. UCLA has vast resources and teams of lawyers preparing to defend their excuse for shutting down a conservative lecture on campus.

**Will you give $50 right now to stand with the conservative students of UCLA and fight back?** We are looking for 76 Americans to step forward today with a gift to protect conservative free speech. **And** **every dollar you give will fuel our fight to ensure that students on EVERY campus can learn the truth about Israel, Hamas, and the freedoms that make America great. **

Here's the secure link where you can quickly make your gift: **[https://secure.yaf.org/ucla-lawsuit-protect-conservative-speech](http://links.newsletter.conservativedirect.com/u/click?_t=5b1853ae48754bee8f471363fe4933a9&_m=1fa28fdbba8946539844ceafdcd135dc&_e=HXPr2cPeK3fWc34pcmSCNUszHXapj1CmeXiHx8uiFuGMo4Gk6cRFdJVlSiSbDzRt2Nt4kV4XJrBl-3v-mF1SRw9QpNYfAAJHH6iajakHrQHacRXq1AP5H1t6dIMO6aYDKDNDfmPFtJ6Lw3uPyd4VL1PdD1b1t5WkFSScoe-JxVySsj5qDK6LsjzQqbETx-Dspl2hi1i45GNxYzjkKPljHagZW3n0j7qQ3W31IVlg48Lm7v4gFB53gBzuNXuHsD7olsrsNonMn5_YEvtoGk0C_AjZCFma4aXC6gexbScVIhA2qXU0sZj_mPjfXOxKIjtq7SOeZjS717nn61jz0b1d-7j5SCt__A-wR9gbviLsFe9bNJqK_327SQf-aMqVr5xpkcYua7UB6esdlwA-Zp5iGg%3D%3D)**

YAF does not play around when students' First Amendment rights are infringed. YAF sued the University of California at Berkeley, and won a major freedom of speech lawsuit!

But they need your support right away!

UCLA and every other leftist university are counting on conservatives like you sitting this fight out. Thank you for taking action right now and fighting back.

Sincerely,

Robert Spencer

body:
Disappointed but not surprised | [](https://click.everyaction.com/k/86636291/478514267/2141984067?sourceid=1149649&utm_campaign=24emfr062407aax&utm_medium=ea&utm_source=email&utm_content=fye&amtOpts=&recurringAmtOpts=&am=&recurringAm=&is_optimized_ask=true&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9DRlJSL0NGUlIvMS85NTk4MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIyYTMwYmExOC00ZTI3LWVmMTEtODZkMi02MDQ1YmRkOWUwOTYiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=13z6MxpWVA9M96x40dBVo4ueO5W-JcgPFj0HMotA21Q=&emci=bfa5475c-1024-ef11-86d2-6045bdd9e096&emdi=2a30ba18-4e27-ef11-86d2-6045bdd9e096&ceid=954237) | [](https://click.everyaction.com/k/86636298/478514285/2141984067?sourceid=1149649&utm_campaign=24emfr062407aax&utm_medium=ea&utm_source=email&utm_content=fye&amtOpts=&recurringAmtOpts=&am=&recurringAm=&is_optimized_ask=true&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9DRlJSL0NGUlIvMS85NTk4MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIyYTMwYmExOC00ZTI3LWVmMTEtODZkMi02MDQ1YmRkOWUwOTYiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=13z6MxpWVA9M96x40dBVo4ueO5W-JcgPFj0HMotA21Q=&emci=bfa5475c-1024-ef11-86d2-6045bdd9e096&emdi=2a30ba18-4e27-ef11-86d2-6045bdd9e096&ceid=954237)
---|---
| Peter,

When I sat down to write an overview of the Texas Supreme Court's opinion in _Zurawski v. Texas,_ I struggled to find the words. [**I am extremely disappointed but not surprised. After all, this is the same court that denied Kate Cox an abortion at the end of last year.**](https://click.everyaction.com/k/86636300/478514289/1859933966?source=24EMFR062407AAX&utm_medium=ea&utm_source=email&utm_campaign=24EMFR062407AAX&utm_content=fye&sourceid=1149649&amtOpts=&recurringAmtOpts=&am=&recurringAm=&is_optimized_ask=true&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9DRlJSL0NGUlIvMS85NTk4MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIyYTMwYmExOC00ZTI3LWVmMTEtODZkMi02MDQ1YmRkOWUwOTYiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=13z6MxpWVA9M96x40dBVo4ueO5W-JcgPFj0HMotA21Q=&emci=bfa5475c-1024-ef11-86d2-6045bdd9e096&emdi=2a30ba18-4e27-ef11-86d2-6045bdd9e096&ceid=954237)

The most shocking thing about the opinion is what isn't there. **The 20 women involved in our case are written out entirely, as if their experiences don't matter.** Where are their names? Where are their real experiences of being denied real, life-saving abortion care in their state?

[**Bringing this case wasn't easy and it's only because of the unfaltering support of people like you that we made it happen.**](https://click.everyaction.com/k/86636302/478514291/1859933966?source=24EMFR062407AAX&utm_medium=ea&utm_source=email&utm_campaign=24EMFR062407AAX&utm_content=fye&sourceid=1149649&amtOpts=&recurringAmtOpts=&am=&recurringAm=&is_optimized_ask=true&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9DRlJSL0NGUlIvMS85NTk4MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIyYTMwYmExOC00ZTI3LWVmMTEtODZkMi02MDQ1YmRkOWUwOTYiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=13z6MxpWVA9M96x40dBVo4ueO5W-JcgPFj0HMotA21Q=&emci=bfa5475c-1024-ef11-86d2-6045bdd9e096&emdi=2a30ba18-4e27-ef11-86d2-6045bdd9e096&ceid=954237) And while I know so many of us are taking this loss very hard, I am celebrating everything we did accomplish.

clean_body: Disappointed but not surprised | | ---|--- | Peter, When I sat down to write an overview of the Texas Supreme Court's opinion in Zurawski v. Texas, I struggled to find the words. The most shocking thing about the opinion is what isn't there. The 20 women involved in our case are written out entirely, as if their experiences don't matter. Where are their names? Where are their real experiences of being denied real, life-saving abortion care in their state? And while I know so many of us are taking this loss very hard, I am celebrating everything we did accomplish. Through this case and others that we filed in the last year, we have helped shift the narrative about abortion bans in the U.S. The phrase, "exceptions don't work" is everywhere. You did that. We did that. body:
Weeks after I was sworn in as a US Senator, I made the decision to seek treatment for depression.
#
Derek,
Weeks after I was sworn in as a US Senator, I made the decision to seek treatment for depression. Asking for help is the hardest step to take sometimes – **but it works.**
Before I sought help for my depression, I was the biggest cynic. As I reflect, the resources and support I received from my care team truly worked and helped me turn my mental health around.
Now, as a Senator and as someone who has been there, I’m committed to ensuring that everyone suffering from mental health challenges has access to the same resources and treatment that I did.
It’s why I partnered with my colleague, Senator Tina Smith, to introduce a bill to establish the Senate Commission on Mental Health. It’s one big step towards achieving my commitment to expand mental health resources.
We’re just getting started on our path, Derek. **[If you share my vision of expanded mental healthcare access for every American, will you contribute $5 to help me see this to the finish line?](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/jf-email-20240610?refcode=em20240610-9094&refcode2=9094_434096_VDUJwI&akid=9094%2E434096%2EVDUJwI)**
**[Donate »](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/jf-email-20240610?amount=5&refcode=em20240610-9094&refcode2=9094_434096_VDUJwI&akid=9094%2E434096%2EVDUJwI)**
My colleagues from both parties were so supportive of my decision to seek help, but there were others that weren’t so kind.
You see, there is a deep rooted negative stigma surrounding mental health in our society. The truth of the matter is that our mental wellbeing is just as important as our physical health – _and should be seen as such!_
I am dedicated to ending the stigma and using the resources I have as a Senator to uplift and expand every Americans’ access to high-quality mental health care.
I am fighting each day to make that a reality, Derek. **[Can I count on your support to keep me in this fight through a $5 contribution?](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/jf-email-20240610?refcode=em20240610-9094&refcode2=9094_434096_VDUJwI&akid=9094%2E434096%2EVDUJwI)**
**[Donate »](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/jf-email-20240610?amount=5&refcode=em20240610-9094&refcode2=9094_434096_VDUJwI&akid=9094%2E434096%2EVDUJwI)**
We’re in this fight together.
❤️ John
John Fetterman
U.S. Senator from Pennsylvania
Even when you’ve won, depression can make you feel like you’ve lost. If you are suffering from depression, please, please get help. Call or text 988 for assistance with suicide prevention + mental health + substance use crises. Help is always available.

Fellow Conservative, _Me?_ A small-town farm girl from Pasco, WA standing in the Oval Office?

Being thanked by President Trump himself for the work I’ve done for our veterans?

It _never_ crossed my mind, n _ever in my wildest dreams_.

Nor did it ever cross my mind that I would be running for a seat in the United States Congress.

But that’s exactly the position I find myself in today.

To understand how we got here, let me tell you a little bit about my story.

April 6, 2005 started like any other day. I went to work as a triage nurse while my husband Scotty was serving our country in Iraq as an infantry officer in the U.S. Army.

_Then, I received the call every military spouse dreads:_**Scotty was in a suicide bomber explosion, and they didn’t know if he was going to make it.**

# VOTE SOBOLESKI TOMORROW!
---
---
| [](https://eqbp6ugbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001uMvNOmz1xRiHrITQ1nDRYALCgUfdoqJuCM7J3T1fGU0IilRM9XmRgd5pAVQS6ohT4dXeJ5ieIkBwohjJvkAOM4GcCs8xYynh2S_xjmn0jKQPfovaW8mdq2j8Yi3lrXU25WULL-4ehZBrtCxHEZrE9GYY1Z8hxOaAklRAw468ePF6Nkwx1cWlhQ==&c=Zaiu6JkuzagWxlV1PbizzPx4UIHSz5ZJyk9m37GHTuIuSECWrLkIlw==&ch=LbtyCaqy9ADR17mSQLjiGGhfP-_cqcxkCSNnRLwzgtT9nzQMsAMrEg==)
---
|
Peter,
Tomorrow, June 11th is voting day. With this election what we have before us is an opportunity. An opportunity to send a real conservative to Congress to fight for us. I've heard for many years that the grassroot Republicans want someone who represents the base to take on Jared Golden. You and only you have the opportunity to make that happen tomorrow by voting Soboleski for CD2.
My voting record is rated 100% by CPAC. I'm the only candidate in this race to have that score. I'm a proud Marine Corps veteran and did my part in New York City after the towers fell in 2001 as a first responder attached to an NYPD-ESU unit. I have done my duty.
In the legislature I'm the only candidate to pick the fights that the base wanted our elected leaders to fight. I fought to keep President Trump on the ballot, I worked to try to impeach Shenna Bellows twice and bar her from administering the 2024 Presidential election. I've stood up at school board meetings and spoke for those who couldn't to protect our kids and defend parents' rights. Principles and policy are my weapons, and I am the conservative fighter in this race.
In terms of lawmaking, I am effective. My bill and 6 months of hard work stopped the EV mandate. I helped to stop our rivers from being polluted and open up responsible lithium mining to economies in western Maine near my district. I have served my state and my community.
I'm the only candidate in this race with 'A' grades from both Gun Owners of Maine and Gun Owners of America. I never have and never will walk out on an important gun vote to go campaign. I am a workhorse, not a show horse.
Let me be perfectly clear. I am proudly Pro-Life and always have been. My 0% rating from Planned Parenthood backs that up. I voted 9/9 against Planned Parenthood bills. My opponent voted 2/9 because he didn't show up to vote. I am the Pro-Life candidate in this race no matter how much mud my opponent slings in my direction to cover up his record.
I am the most conservative, experienced and qualified candidate in this race for the Republican nomination for CD2. I will not be pushed around in Washington D.C. I've worked hard, fought the fights that needed to be fought and got important legislation passed against the odds.
My campaign has taken zero PAC money. I owe the Swamp nothing.
I am asking you for your vote tomorrow Tuesday, June 11th because I believe I've earned it. I thank you for your support and ask you to please get out and vote for Mike Soboleski tomorrow!
Stay Safe, Mike
P.S. I'll be on the George Hale/Ric Tyler radio show tomorrow at 7:30am I hope you'll tune in!

body:
# [](https://act.hillharper.com/go/421?t=1&akid=1265%2E62735%2E6FTcog)
| | | Dear Peter, We stand at a critical crossroads for Michigan's future, and the choice has never been clearer. It’s time to elect a Senator who truly fights for our values. Hill Harper is that leader. Unlike Elissa Slotkin, Hill is unwavering in his commitment to real Democratic principles and the needs of our communities.

**Elissa Slotkin's record is a betrayal to us all:** **Against Student Debt Relief:** Slotkin turned her back on countless struggling Michiganders by opposing $10,000 relief on private loans.

**Against Medicare for All:** She failed to support the Medicare for All Act, ignoring the desperate need for comprehensive healthcare reform.

**Against Marijuana Decriminalization:** Despite Michigan voters approving recreational marijuana, Slotkin didn’t back the Marijuana Opportunity Reinvestment and Expungement Act.

**Against Justice:** She was the only Michigan Democrat not to cosponsor the George Floyd Justice and Policing Act, abandoning our communities of color in their call for justice.

**Corporate Ties:** Slotkin accepted $2,800 from conservative mega-donor Harlan Crow, raising serious questions about her loyalties.

**Against Labor and Education:** She opposed measures for labor fairness and was the only Democrat to vote against increasing funds for the National Center for College Students with Disabilities.

**Against the Green New Deal:** Slotkin defended obstructionist Senators Manchin and Sinema, undermining progressive legislation.

**Misleading on Abortion:** Despite her pro-choice district, Slotkin falsely claimed it was pro-life.

**Against Gun Control:** She initially opposed advancing critical gun control bills, stalling efforts to tackle gun violence effectively. Slotkin's record is clear: she is not the Democrat she claims to be. She does not represent the interests of Michigan's working families, students, or marginalized communities. **We need a Senator who will fight for us, not against us.**

Hill Harper is a true progressive who will champion Medicare for All, fight for student debt relief, stand up for social justice, and tirelessly protect our environment and reproductive rights. **He believes in a Michigan where everyone has the opportunity to thrive.** **[**Join us in supporting Hill Harper for the United States Senate. Your contribution today will help us build a future where every voice is heard, and every vote truly matters.**](https://act.hillharper.com/go/1721?t=2&akid=1265%2E62735%2E6FTcog)**

I’ve got to get my fundraising on track, to make sure we win this race. I’m writing you today to ask for one dollar. One dollar may not seem like much, but when combined with thousands of dollars from other supporters, it all adds up to a winning campaign. I don’t have a network of deep-pocketed tech billionaires and special interest lobbyists to bail my campaign out at the last minute -- I count on support from you and millions more grassroots Republicans like you to fund my campaign. Your support enables me to hold grassroots campaign events, create advertising campaigns to spread my conservative message, and travel across the Lowcountry to meet and talk with voters. If grassroots Republicans give up on me, I will have to close down my campaign giving the D.C. establishment a MAJOR victory. Thank you, Nancy Mace P.S. I know money is tight, but truly one dollar can make a difference in a campaign like mine because these races come down to the last minute and the last dollar. , please know how thankful I am for your support, and I hope to continue to make you proud in Congress. | | About Nancy Congresswoman Nancy Mace grew up in the Lowcountry. She is the daughter of a retired Army General and retired school teacher. She is a proud mother of two, the first female to graduate from The Citadel's Corps of Cadets, and a tough conservative who wants to save our country from the radicals who hate America! | | We can’t let this continue: Republican extremists are using mass challenges to scare voters and suppress our voices — and we need to keep calling out their bad behavior. Here’s how mass challenges work:
* Someone claims that a voter in their county isn’t properly registered, submitting what’s referred to as a “challenge” to their county board of elections.
* When that challenge process is set in motion, the person whose eligibility and qualifications are challenged must jump through hoops to stay on the list of registered voters.
* The overwhelming majority of challenges have been dismissed due to faulty evidence, but the point is to suppress the vote by creating unnecessary burdens for eligible voters and county officials.

The Fair Fight team has been spreading the word here in Georgia about mass challenges and working to hold bad actors accountable for years now, but their suppressive tactics are gaining speed in other states like Michigan, Texas, and Pennsylvania. Right wing groups are even promoting their challenge tactics, raising money to organize off the concept. **It’s a coordinated grassroots effort to purge the nation’s voter rolls ahead of the 2024 elections.** [**Your gift of $25 today can help Fair Fight combat voter suppression and ensure access to the ballot box.**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/86643972/478541812/-1658962082?amount=25&refcode=bsc_emm_ff_20240610_f_VoterChallenges101_v1s2&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNDMvMS84ODQ1MCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJiYTJlMmI3OC02MTI3LWVmMTEtODZkMi02MDQ1YmRkOWUwOTYiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=oDFztN_D9GNmoZ_yPM5oYUe7PCgY7PS_wUnpmNL6Foc=) The use of mass voter challenges to intimidate voters is a historic Georgia tradition going back to Reconstruction and carrying through to Jim Crow. In the aftermath of historic turnout in the 2020 election, right wing groups are doubling down on their efforts to intimidate voters and keep them from the polls. And don’t forget: in 2021, Georgia Republicans passed a law making it easier for private citizens to challenge the eligibility and qualifications of an unlimited number of voters within their county. The student organizers asked Jill and the team to intercede with university officials to try to de-escalate the situation. A total of six police departments assembled on the scene. The cops advanced on the protesters and used their bicycles as weapons, eventually knocking Jill to the ground. The American people are learning what Trump said about our wounded and fallen warriors, and they do not like what they are hearing.
#
At a rally in Nevada, Trump finally responded to the reports that he insulted the fallen when he canceled an appearance at an American war cemetery in France.
He said you’d have to be a psycho to call Americans who fell in battle “suckers” and “losers,” and we agree.
But that comment is quite odd, given that he called Americans who fell in battle “suckers” and “losers.” His own former Chief of Staff confirmed it. Personally.
Remember:
* Trump attacked John McCain and every Prisoner of War — “I like people who weren’t captured” — and called him a loser after he had passed away.
* He said, “It doesn’t look good for me,” and refused to be seen with wounded warriors.
* He’s gone after Gold Star family members, who lost their loved ones in war, for opposing him.
* He callously told one grieving wife that her husband “knew what he was getting into.”

There is a clear, repeated pattern of Trump going after Troops, Veterans and their families.
But of all the despicable things Trump has done, his insults and degradations against the wounded and fallen men and women who fought for our country are among the worst.
But what’s clear is this — he knows this hurts him. He might weasel out of jail time for his felonies, or delay his court cases thanks to judges he appointed. But the American people are learning what Trump said about our wounded and fallen warriors, and they do not like what they are hearing.
We have to make sure they keep hearing it, and that’s exactly what VoteVets is going to do.

#
Friend of Life,

My name is Lila Rose. I'm the founder and president of Live Action.

Today Live Action is the online, educational leader of the pro-life movement. We reach millions of Americans each month--changing minds and hearts and saving lives.

I wanted to alert you about a growing threat to preborn babies, one that is contributing to the growth in abortion numbers this year.

That's right. Even though _Roe v. Wade_ is gone, abortion rates are _growing_ instead of decreasing. Reports say that a preborn child in the United States now loses its life every 31 seconds.

And, corporate America has decided to jump on board and expand the killing.

**You see, at least 114 big corporations are paying --often pressuring--their female employees to fly to pro-abortion "sanctuary" states like California to kill their preborn children.**

Corporations like Amazon, Nike, Uber, Target, Disney, Starbucks, Sony, eBay, CVS, Apple, Bank of America, and 103 others are offering women $4,000, $5,000, $10,000, or unlimited "travel" and "lodging" to go abort their children.

It's beyond sickening.

body:
The journey towards gender equality is far from over, especially here in Missouri. Peter,

The Equal Pay Act of 1963 was a groundbreaking decision that aimed to ensure men and women receive equal pay for equal work. While this was a crucial step forward for gender equity – _our journey is far from complete._

Sadly, Missouri ranks **12th** in the country for having the widest gender pay gap. **Women in Missouri earn an average of $45,034 annually, which is 20.9% less than the $56,983 earned by men.** This means women are earning just 79 cents for every dollar that white men earn, a gap that is even larger for women of color, who face even more severe disparities simply for the color of their skin.

These numbers represent more than just statistics. They reflect real struggles and lost opportunities for women and families throughout Missouri. The gender pay gap means less money for essentials like housing, education, and healthcare, and it perpetuates economic insecurity for countless women, and their families, all across our state.

But Peter, gender equality is more than a principle; it’s a necessity. Equal pay for equal work is a fundamental right, and we must continue pushing for policies that reflect the core values of our democracy, starting with electing leaders like Wesley Bell, who will always stand up for every-day people.

Wesley is committed to closing the gender pay gap in Congress, and will always vote to ensure that women in Missouri – _including thousands here in St. Louis_ – are afforded the same opportunities, respect, and pay as their white, male counterparts.

| June is National Gun Violence Awareness Month, a time to reflect on the urgent need to protect our communities from gun violence.

As West Michigan’s representative and a member of the Gun Violence Prevention Task Force, I have dedicated my first year in Congress to safeguarding our communities. In my first term, I’ve worked tirelessly to advocate for gun violence prevention legislation, including an assault weapons ban.

This month, I reaffirm my commitment to creating a safer environment for our children and communities.

Thank you for your unwavering support and commitment to ensuring a safer West Michigan.

Gratefully,

Hillary

body:
We cannot allow hate to legislate.

| [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/86646720/478551452/568840269?refcode=BLU_EM_CBC_2024-06-10_1&amount=25&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTAvMS8xMDUwMDUiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiNmYwY2YyNTEtNjgyNy1lZjExLTg2ZDItNjA0NWJkZDllMDk2IiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=MwH-CS2f1lMWQs9QY5wp2Z7frWzxsRuU-HSK3kdRij8=)

| Peter,

June is nationally recognized as Pride Month — a time to celebrate the contributions of the LGBTQ+ community. It’s also a time to honor the progress we’ve made and recognize the work that still lies ahead in realizing the promises of America.

As a mom and former English teacher, I know how to spot a bully. I also know how frustrating it can be to feel unseen and unaccepted. That's why it deeply concerns me when I see politicians spend all their time **interfering** in people’s lives instead of working to **improve** them.

Let’s be clear—we cannot allow politicians to dismantle civil liberties and undermine our democracy. This month, let’s take time to think about the Americans serving in our armed forces for a safer America even as they feel less safe, and let’s remember all of those who have fought and died for this country for the promise of freedom—for people to live how they want to live and love who they want to love.

**We cannot allow hate to legislate.**

So, this month, we embrace the fact that by protecting civil liberties for some, we protect them for all. And let’s hold tight to simple truths I tell my kids all the time: **“You are loved” is a full sentence; being loud doesn’t make you right; kindness is not weakness.**

Tuebor,

Callie

clean_body: We cannot allow hate to legislate. | = | Peter, June is nationally recognized as Pride Month — a time to celebrate the contributions of the LGBTQ+ community. It’s also a time to honor the progress we’ve made and recognize the work that still lies ahead in realizing the promises of America. As a mom and former English teacher, I know how to spot a bully. I also know how frustrating it can be to feel unseen and unaccepted. That's why it deeply concerns me when I see politicians spend all their time interfering in people’s lives instead of working to improve them. Let’s be clear—we cannot allow politicians to dismantle civil liberties and undermine our democracy. This month, let’s take time to think about the Americans serving in our armed forces for a safer America even as they feel less safe, and let’s remember all of those who have fought and died for this country for the promise of freedom—for people to live how they want to live and love who they want to love. We cannot allow hate to legislate. So, this month, we embrace the fact that by protecting civil liberties for some, we protect them for all. And let’s hold tight to simple truths I tell my kids all the time: “You are loved” is a full sentence; being loud doesn’t make you right; kindness is not weakness. Hello,
Every time I see a new attack on abortion rights and women’s reproductive freedoms, I think of my dad.
For the first few years of my life, my family lived on an Indian reservation in Northern Montana. Dad was an OB-GYN – in the years before _Roe v. Wade_ ...
[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/86647316/478553046/1610638071?refcode=em20240610am-nd&amounts=5%2C10%2C25%2C35%2C50%2C100%2C250&refcode2=4ad76450-6927-ef11-86d2-6045bdd9e096&recurring=true&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzMvMS85NjIxNiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI0YWQ3NjQ1MC02OTI3LWVmMTEtODZkMi02MDQ1YmRkOWUwOTYiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=RK3RzRYwjV4VuEUC2Am0uR5Ro8Al12kObC8OXyRQKP0=)
Years later, Dad recounted how he saw patients that came from all walks of life. Black, brown, and white. Younger and older. Rich and poor. And just as many Republicans walked through his doors as did Democrats.
Looking back, having a father who provided women with access to health care – especially at a time when so many were being denied the right – really shaped how I think about the issue.
My dad is in his 80’s and retired now, but for years, he helped train the next generation of health care providers at Planned Parenthood. And my sister, who later also became an OB-GYN, is continuing on his legacy.
**Extremists like Lauren Boebert and my new Republican opponents want you to think that women having the freedom to make their own medical decisions is some extreme idea. It’s not.**
What’s extreme is pushing a bill in Congress that would make all abortions illegal – including in cases of rape or incest – and wanting to ban a medication that’s been approved for decades for abortions and miscarriages.
Their views are a fringe one – supported by people who think that the government should be dictating women’s medical decisions, instead of allowing women the freedom to make choices with their doctor.
I would have thought that after almost losing this seat last year, they might have at least pretended to moderate on this issue. But they've only doubled down on the extreme.
**Only 546 votes separated Lauren Boebert and me in 2022, and I’m ready to finish the job in 2024 by winning this seat and replacing her in Congress.**
[**Please, if you’re able to, will you consider chipping in to my campaign today to help me win this critical House seat and replace Lauren Boebert in Congress? Our race was the closest in the country, but I’m not taking money from corporate PACs. I’m counting on grassroots donors like you if I’m going to win.**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/86647317/478553047/1610638071?refcode=em20240610am-nd&amounts=5%2C10%2C25%2C35%2C50%2C100%2C250&refcode2=4ad76450-6927-ef11-86d2-6045bdd9e096&recurring=true&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzMvMS85NjIxNiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI0YWQ3NjQ1MC02OTI3LWVmMTEtODZkMi02MDQ1YmRkOWUwOTYiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=RK3RzRYwjV4VuEUC2Am0uR5Ro8Al12kObC8OXyRQKP0=)

clean_body: Every time I see a new attack on abortion rights and women’s reproductive freedoms, I think of my dad. Hello, Every time I see a new attack on abortion rights and women’s reproductive freedoms, I think of my dad. For the first few years of my life, my family lived on an Indian reservation in Northern Montana. Dad was an OB-GYN – in the years before Roe v. Wade ... = Years later, Dad recounted how he saw patients that came from all walks of life. Black, brown, and white. Younger and older. Rich and poor. And just as many Republicans walked through his doors as did Democrats. Looking back, having a father who provided women with access to health care – especially at a time when so many were being denied the right – really shaped how I think about the issue. My dad is in his 80’s and retired now, but for years, he helped train the next generation of health care providers at Planned Parenthood. And my sister, who later also became an OB-GYN, is continuing on his legacy. Extremists like Lauren Boebert and my new Republican opponents want you to think that women having the freedom to make their own medical decisions is some extreme idea. It’s not. What’s extreme is pushing a bill in Congress that would make all abortions illegal – including in cases of rape or incest – and wanting to ban a medication that’s been approved for decades for abortions and miscarriages. Their views are a fringe one – supported by people who think that the government should be dictating women’s medical decisions, instead of allowing women the freedom to make choices with their doctor. I would have thought that after almost losing this seat last year, they might have at least pretended to moderate on this issue. But they've only doubled down on the extreme. Only 546 votes separated Lauren Boebert and me in 2022, and I’m ready to finish the job in 2024 by winning this seat and replacing her in Congress. = Please use the links in this email to start a monthly donation through ActBlue: | | = | = | | = | = | | = | = Thank you for letting me share some of my story with you. Thank you for having the courage and integrity to report the corruption and lawbreaking you saw while serving as state employees.
You will get plenty of thanks as you begin on this journey. You will get plenty of harassment and baseless hatred, too.
Those of us who pay attention to corruption in Florida knew that DeSantis' administration hid records of the Governor's use of public resources during his failed and humiliating campaign for President.
His use of state police and state funds for out-of-state campaign trips absolutely falls under the purview of Florida's Sunshine laws, and you did your duty by reporting pressure from his administration to keep those records secret.
If you're careful in protecting yourself, the story will remain fixed on that - the misuse of public funds for a doomed Presidential campaign and the illegal tactics used to keep it secret.
However, if the recent Politico article is any indication, DeSantis' administration will use the same depraved attacks on you that they did on me. And they will do it so that the conversation is about anything other than what you reported.
They have already sought to defame you in the media with false and irrelevant accusations of illicit sexual affairs.
They will call you insubordinate, accuse you of creating a "difficult" workplace environment, and question your credentials.
They weaponized state law enforcement against you, attempted to file bogus criminal charges against you, and had police investigate your entire lives - just to leak the 129-page report to the media so those allegations would reach the public.
And the harassment will not stop. It will not dampen with time. It will not stop when you win the first investigation, the second, the third or the fourth. It will not dampen when you win a settlement or win at court. It will go on forever.
I hope you endure less of it than I have. I doubt you will be raided at gunpoint, your children terrorized and arrested on equally false pretenses, your names repeatedly drug through the mud at DeSantis' unhinged press conferences.
They have learned from coming after me what works and what doesn't. They will find your vulnerabilities, hurt those you care most about, and try to drive you insane.
The entire world will seem upside down.
I hope someone told you that blowing the whistle means you'll probably never work in the same careers again.
I hope someone told you that your lawsuits will likely take years, be continually delayed, and that the state will obstruct at every possible turn.
I hope someone told you that, unless you have a wealthy family, you will likely be completely broke in a few years -- if not sooner.
I hope someone told you that Florida is no longer a safe place for you - especially now that you know state police are after you.
I hope someone told you that once the world moves on, you will still be suffering.
I hope someone told you that the price for integrity may very well be your sanity.
Above all else, I hope you stick to your guns and don't let these bastards win.
From one whistleblower to another, thank you.

The clock is ticking. Right now, hundreds of thousands of DACA recipients and DACA-eligible young people are awaiting a critical decision in a lawsuit seeking to end the DACA program.
Tens of thousands of people have relied on DACA to be able to work as nurses, teachers, entrepreneurs, and valued employees, and in the process strengthened our communities and our economy.
_Yet our ability to work and live in the country we call home is under threat because of a small contingent of right-wing politicians hellbent on putting our lives at stake for their own political agendas._
It is Congressional inaction that has led us to this moment.
It is Congressional inaction that has left the DACA program vulnerable to attacks from the far-right.
**So now it is up to Congress to deliver.** DACA was never meant to be a permanent solution. After 12 years of temporary band-aids, it’s time for legislation to permanently protect immigrant youth.

United We Dream Action has set a goal to raise $12,000 ahead of the anniversary on Saturday — and last we checked, we’re 34% of the way there. Right now, hundreds of thousands of DACA recipients and DACA-eligible young people are awaiting a critical decision in a lawsuit seeking to end the DACA program. Tens of thousands of people have relied on DACA to be able to work as nurses, teachers, entrepreneurs, and valued employees, and in the process strengthened our communities and our economy. Yet our ability to work and live in the country we call home is under threat because of a small contingent of right-wing politicians hellbent on putting our lives at stake for their own political agendas. FROM: A grateful Democrat
Subject: I’m so grateful.

**Dear President Biden,

I’m so thankful for everything you’ve done as President!

**Despite MAGA turmoil, over the last three years, you’ve fought TIRELESSLY for the American people — defending abortion rights, confirming an incredible Supreme Court Justice, saving Social Security from GOP cuts, and creating millions of jobs for the people.**

I know standing up to MAGA Republican attacks isn’t easy, but it is always the right thing to do.

So as the 2024 race kicks into high gear, I wanted to show my support and thank you for being such an amazing leader for our country!

Hi folks, Senator Tammy Baldwin here.
This month marks 55 years since the New York City Police Department raided Stonewall Inn, a bar in the city’s Greenwich Village and safe haven for the LGBTQ+ community.
Several brave Americans, led by Black and brown trans activists, fought back against police violence and harassment. Demonstrations throughout the city happened over the span of six days, kickstarting the modern LGBTQ+ movement for equal rights.
Stonewall is a story of those who came before us and put everything on the line in a demand to be treated with dignity and respect. Those who bravely stood up and spoke out so that others wouldn’t have to live in fear or silence.
Progress was made possible by the Black and brown trans activists who have always been on the frontlines of the fight for LGBTQ+ rights. We must never forget that.
I’m inspired by how far we’ve come in the past 55 years, but as Republicans continue their assault on LGBTQ+ rights — targeting and dehumanizing trans kids, banning LGBTQ+ discussion in our schools, and even threatening to overturn Supreme Court decisions that granted our right to marriage equality — it’s clear there is so much more work to be done.

body:
The majority of women in Tennessee are pro-choice.

| | | | | [ ](https://zg05qvsd.r.us-east-2.awstrack.me/L0/https:%2F%2Fourtenn.org%2F/1/010f019004282fae-7bf56fc1-e350-4b4c-a4fd-90fe176d9fd7-000000/560P1h7eeq3qd0H4axZmxl5X-5w=162)
---
Dear Peter,
---
| | Women are fleeing the state.

Doctors have to choose between letting a pregnant woman die... or jail time.

Tennessee is forcing women into life-threatening situations due to extreme abortion bans and shockingly narrow medical exceptions. Doctors hesitate to provide critical care, fearing harsh legal repercussions. Women suffer; their health and lives at risk.

**This isn’t just politics - it’s life and death.**[**It is up to us to protect women in Tennessee.**](https://zg05qvsd.r.us-east-2.awstrack.me/L0/https:%2F%2Fsecure.actblue.com%2Fdonate%2Four-tennessee-future-pac-1%3Frefcode=TENN_24_EM_15_ProChoiceTennessee/1/010f019004282fae-7bf56fc1-e350-4b4c-a4fd-90fe176d9fd7-000000/gQYt-FNJ6gxmLWsDkBCdokh4jY0=162)****

Vanderbilt University recently conducted a statewide poll and found that the majority of Tennessee women are pro-choice.

Yet our voices are being silenced.

This is why we need to elect Champions for Choice.

Allie Phillips is on the front lines, advocating for reproductive rights and challenging these draconian laws.

🔹 Allie’s Promise: As a staunch advocate for women’s health, she has vowed to fight tirelessly for the right to safe and accessible abortion care.
🔹 Allie’s Vision: A Tennessee where every woman can make her own healthcare decisions without fear or restriction.

**But Allie’s dedication isn’t just political—it’s deeply personal. **When Allie faced a complicated pregnancy, she made the difficult decision to have an abortion. It was a choice that saved her life and one she believes every woman should be able to make without government interference.

Allie Phillips represents the change we need. Her dedication to reproductive rights is unwavering, and with your support, we can help her win this crucial battle.

Dear Peter,
Why am I running?
Because I don’t like the way the country is going.
And I know millions of Americans don’t either.
I don’t like the wars.
I don’t like the censorship.
I don’t like the addiction to war — both political parties are now the war party.
I don’t like the corporate capture of our government — the corrupt merger of state and corporate power.

At a time when state courts and legislatures are restricting abortion access, IVF, and contraceptives across the map, this blatant and outright refusal to protect basic women’s autonomy is just one more way that our legislators are infringing on our most basic rights. | | | [](https://click.everyaction.com/k/86651910/478569241/-1153425267?refcode=6-7-24&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAxNS8xLzkwOTg3IiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogIjhhMzg2ZmJmLTc3MjctZWYxMS04NmQyLTYwNDViZGQ5ZTA5NiIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=3qeh-NRh4DxtWzDYpuyGqYk-OGYl9lEVHWIdmnAthnE=)

At a time when state courts and legislatures are restricting abortion access, IVF, and contraceptives across the map, this blatant and outright refusal to protect basic women’s autonomy is just one more way that our legislators are infringing on our most basic rights. The vast majority of Americans are in favor of protecting access to contraception, so it’s completely ridiculous that Republicans opposed this bill. Republican Senators are supposed to represent the will of their constituents, and in this instance, they are playing up to special interests and the far-right, not the people in their states. **[**This entire issue boils down to the fact that our courts are being infiltrated by the influence of conservative mega-donors and they have finally eroded one of our most crucial rights: the right to bodily autonomy. If you think that our judicial system needs to be reformed to root out this partisan political influence, join us in the fight by chipping in $10 right now.**](https://click.everyaction.com/k/86651911/478569250/-1153425267?refcode=6-7-24&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAxNS8xLzkwOTg3IiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogIjhhMzg2ZmJmLTc3MjctZWYxMS04NmQyLTYwNDViZGQ5ZTA5NiIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=3qeh-NRh4DxtWzDYpuyGqYk-OGYl9lEVHWIdmnAthnE=)** All the way up to the Supreme Court, our judicial system is corrupt, and it’s no secret.
